newsitem.title: JAPAN: Deutsche Telekom sees small merits in NTT break-up.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Telekom sees small merits in NTT break-up.

text.p: A Japanese unit of German telecom monopoly Deutsche Telekom AG, said that a planned break-up of NTT Corp would bring little benefits to rival carriers or subscribers in Japan.
"I personally see no advantage (in the break-up plan)," Deutsche Telekom K.K. president Paul Kuhn told Reuters in a recent interview.
"I can't see if there will be more competition between NTT's two regional companies...I don't see if carriers like us will have better local access to NTT's network," Kuhn said.

The Japanese government late last year announced a plan to break up Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp into one international and long-distance operator and two regional operators under a holding company in 1998 or 1999.

Analysts believe the plan, together with a new interconnection rule requiring NTT to give rival carriers fair access to its network, would open up Japan's telecom market more to foreign and domestic competition.
But Kuhn said he was concerned the break-up plan could make future negotiations with NTT more difficult and time-consuming.
"It may even turn out to be more difficult for us as we will have to negotiate (on local access issues) with two regional operators, instead of one company." he said.

Deregulation and a fast expansion of Japan's telecom market, however, will give Deutsche Telekom a chance to move into multimedia services, such as electronic commerce and electronic publishing, in partnership with Japanese companies, Kuhn said.
"We would try to go into financial partnership (with Japanese companies) with the time frame of this year," he said.
But Japan's decision to lift restrictions on foreign ownership in Japanese telecom carriers would not affect its investment strategy, Kuhn said.
"With Japan's high costs and high share prices, maybe we will have to settle with less (than 51 percent)," Kuhn said.
Deutsche Telekom, which listed its shares on the Tokyo Stock Exchange November 1996, currently offers leased line services between Germany and Japan to more than 120 corporate customers.
